title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: Last week a student told your assistant their major, and today, in a new session, the assistant mentions it. Which explanation of how this works is correct?

options.text: The model's weights were updated by last week's chat
The program saved a note and loaded it into context
The model keeps a private memory for each user
The model recalled it from its original training data

items.stem: One request runs three model calls. The system prompt and tool definitions are 1,000 tokens and the student's question is 50 tokens. After call 1 the model requests a tool (50 tokens) and the result is 400 tokens. After call 2 it requests another tool (50 tokens) and the result is 1,000 tokens. Call 3 writes the final answer. Each call is sent the full transcript so far. How many input tokens in total are sent across the three calls?

Your assistant answers well with 3 manual chunks in context but gets worse when a teammate raises the search result to 60 chunks, although all of them fit in the window. Which statement best explains this?

options.text: Chunks beyond the third are ignored by the model entirely
Sixty chunks cause the window to be reset for the next call
More tokens in context can lower recall, even when they fit
Search results lose their meaning when there are many of them

items.stem: With a client-side memory tool, the model decides to save a note. In one sentence, what actually writes the note to storage, and what does the model receive back?
You are choosing between searching the manuals once before the first model call, and giving the model a search tool it can call repeatedly. What is the main trade-off of the repeated-search tool?

options.text: It makes the manuals part of the model's training data
It is faster, because the model reads the whole manual at once
It removes the need to split manuals into smaller chunks
It can refine a poor query, but takes more calls and tokens
